lines.text: Eleven at night. Forty seven people waiting. Three experts online, all on a call. Twelve more offline, and nobody told them.
An on-demand marketplace for live expert sessions. Astrology, mental health, relationship and financial coaching. Three million downloads, three hundred vetted experts.
The marketplace had no mechanism for what happens when fifty customers arrive at eleven and three experts are free.
The queue grows. Customers leave. Experts never know the demand was there. And the platform absorbs the whole cost of that mismatch, in lost revenue, in dropout, in trust.
At foodpanda I raised the incentive and riders appeared. You cannot do that to a therapist. But those twelve never declined. Nobody asked them.
So I designed Equilibrium. Something that detected the imbalance early, responded automatically, and paid for itself, before the marketplace had an engineering team to build it.
Five modules. Demand signals, health scoring, surge pricing, incentives, and a router that decides what a human has to handle.
Either trigger crossing prices the surge and pushes every expert who can help. Every dollar of that surge is ring fenced to pay them.
Replayed against a real evening: red at minute eight, supply closed within four minutes of detection.
Queue peak down forty eight percent. Delay from thirty four minutes to eighteen. Net cost to the platform, forty dollars.
Watch the full film, then go and drive it yourself.
